project: Agentic AI System for Data Pipeline Incident Investigation

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a pipeline incident, when logs are analyzed, then a recommendation is generated.
Given a log with no common patterns, when analyzed, then no recommendation is generated.
Trust: All log analysis activities are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Pattern catalog covers schema-mismatch and resource-exhaustion signatures only (the two fixtures provided). A log with a real but uncataloged failure (data_engineering_incident_test_3.json) correctly yields no recommendation -- broadening the catalog is follow-on work, not a gap in this story's contract.

criteria.text: Given an investigation, when it is conducted, then all activities are logged.
Given a failed investigation, when it is logged, then failure details are included.
Trust: Logs are immutable and timestamped.

stories.notes: Immutability is hash-chained (each entry embeds the previous entry's hash); verify_log_integrity() detects edited, deleted, or reordered entries. Known gap, documented in audit_log.py's module docstring: truncating the *most recent* entries and re-chaining from there is not detectable without an external anchor (e.g. publishing the latest hash outside this file) -- out of scope for this walking skeleton. 'Unauthorized access to logs' (a listed failure path) is a filesystem/RBAC concern with no auth system yet in this project (REQ-018 is unfulfilled) -- not addressed by this story, flagged rather than silently skipped.

criteria.text: Given a SQL query, when analyzed, then potential issues are identified.
Given a SQL query with no issues, when analyzed, then no issues are reported.
Trust: SQL analysis results are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Issue catalog: select_star, missing_where_on_mutation, cartesian_join, undefined_column (checked against schema_history.current_schema when the incident has one). The undefined_column check independently rediscovers fixture one's actual root cause (customer_type vs customer_category) from the SQL alone; fixture two's real, clean query is the 'no issues' case -- no synthetic fixture needed for either acceptance criterion. Reuses STORY-002's hash-chained audit_log.record_activity rather than a second logging path. 'Performance degradation' (a listed failure path) is not addressed -- no real SQL engine exists to benchmark against in this walking skeleton; noted rather than silently skipped.

criteria.text: Given data-quality metrics, when analyzed, then root causes are identified.
Given data with no quality issues, when analyzed, then no root causes are reported.
Trust: Data-quality analysis results are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Issue catalog: row_count_shortfall (between adjacent pipeline layers), null_rate_high, duplicate_rate_high, schema_drift (unexpected/missing columns), freshness_violation. No synthetic fixture needed: fixture one's real metrics independently flag both the silver-layer row collapse and the schema drift (its actual root cause); fixture two's real metrics flag the gold-layer shortfall, high null rate, and staleness (its actual root cause -- resource exhaustion causing a partial, stale write); fixture three's sparse metrics (connection-timeout incident, no data ever extracted) correctly yield zero issues, serving as the 'no quality issues' case. Reuses STORY-002's hash-chained audit_log.record_activity unchanged. 'Performance issues' (a listed failure path) is not addressed, same reasoning as STORY-003's 'performance degradation' -- no real data platform exists here to benchmark against.

criteria.text: Given a recommendation, when it is major, then it requires human approval.
Given a minor recommendation, when generated, then it is auto-approved.
Trust: All recommendations and approvals are logged.
Given an uncertain root cause, when identified, then a notification is sent.
Given a certain root cause, when identified, then no notification is sent.
Trust: Notifications are logged for audit.
Given an ops team member, when accessing the dashboard, then the primary action completes in three clicks or fewer.
Given an ops team member, when using the interface, then response times are under 2 seconds for any action.
Trust: Given any user action, when logged, then the audit trail records the action with a timestamp.
Given an investigation, when completed, then a detailed report is generated.
Given a failed investigation, when reported, then failure details are included.
Trust: Reports are logged for audit.
Given a pilot test, when conducted, then error rates are low.
Given a pilot test, when completed, then investigation time is reduced to 1 hour.
Trust: Pilot test results are logged for audit.
Given a set of pipeline dependencies, when agents are coordinated, then the analysis completes successfully.
Given a failure in agent coordination, when retried, then the system recovers without data loss.
Trust: Given any coordination task, when executed, then the audit trail logs the task with a timestamp.

stories.notes: coordinate_agents() runs the three existing specialists (investigate() / investigate_sql() / investigate_data_quality()) against one incident, catching only each specialist's own typed exceptions so one agent failing does not stop the others -- overall status is success / partial_failure / failure depending on how many of the three succeeded. Two audit activities (coordination_initiated, agent_coordination) reuse STORY-002's hash-chained record_activity unchanged; both are idempotent on (correlation_id, activity), so retrying coordinate_agents with the same correlation_id after a failure is safe and does not duplicate or lose audit entries. Typed CoordinationInitiationError covers the initial audit write failing before any agent runs; typed CoordinationAuditError covers the summary write failing after agents have already run, and carries the computed results on partial_result rather than discarding them. An unexpected (untyped) exception from an agent is deliberately not caught -- it propagates instead of being masked as a generic failure, which is this design's answer to the 'analysis results are incorrect' failure path: the coordinator can't verify correctness itself, but it won't hide a real bug.
